TOP NEWS " Joshua Jahn: Federal officials identify North Texas man as Dallas ICE shooting suspect," Dallas Morning News' Lilly Kersh \-- "Federal officials named Joshua Jahn, a 29-year-old unemployed Collin County college dropout, as the at the Dallas Immigration and Customs Enforcement facility, and wounding two others before fatally shooting himself. Acting U.S. Attorney Nancy Larson told reporters Thursday Jahn acted alone in what she described as a "." Investigators found a collection of notes at the suspect's home, Larson said, which indicated he intended to "maximize lethality" against -- not target detainees. No law enforcement were injured in the shooting. He hoped his actions would give ICE agents "," induce stress in their lives, and interfere with their work, which he called human trafficking, Larson said. Notes described a hatred for the federal government and called ICE employees "people showing up to collect a dirty paycheck." Public records show Joshua Jahn owned a 2016 Toyota parked outside of a building near the ICE office, located in the 8100 block of North Stemmons Freeway. Police believe the Jahn "indiscriminately" fired rounds from a long-range rifle from the roof of the building in a targeted, ambush-style attack. Bullets hit the facility and transport vans outside the office. Larson said Jahn's car was seen with a large ladder hours before the shooting. Noah Jahn , the suspect's brother, told that Joshua Jahn was not interested in politics and had not voiced opposition to ICE. He said his brother was unemployed and planning to move onto their parents' property in Oklahoma. Noah Jahn did not respond to a phone call from The Dallas Morning News requesting comment. Joseph Rothrock , the agent in charge of the Dallas field office, said the gunfire Wednesday is being investigated as "an act of ." Investigators say the words "ANTI-ICE" were written on an unspent round found Wednesday morning at the . On Wednesday afternoon, police barricaded the street outside his family's home on a leafy block in , a town about 32 miles north of Dallas between Allen and McKinney. Officers in tactical vests, including agents from the FBI, monitored the premises as the home was searched. Federal officials confirmed Jahn legally obtained the rifle he used in the shooting in August. In a post on Facebook made in 2022, the suspect's mother criticized Texas' gun laws, accusing state leaders of not addressing and failing residents.Sharon Jahn quoted a song byJacques Brel in one post. "If we only have love / We can melt all the guns / And then give the new world / To our daughters and sons," the post stated. The family lives near Allen, the site of a at a shopping mall where a gunman fatally shot eight people and injured others. FBI Director Kash Patel said that the FBI has been analyzing devices, data and writings recovered from the home of the suspect. Patel said the subject, who he did not identify by name, downloaded a document containing a list of Department of Homeland Security facilities, searched several times for "ballistics" and for the video of Charlie Kirk 's in the days before the shooting and last month searched several apps that tracks the movements of ICE agents, all of which Patel said showed a "high degree" of pre-planning in the attack. Patel also said investigators found a handwritten note saying, "Hopefully this will give ICE agents real terror, to think, 'is there a sniper with AP rounds on that roof?" Authorities are investigating . Larson said Jahn likely deleted evidence from his devices, and investigators did not find evidence of membership to specific groups. Jahn's LinkedIn profile listed volunteer work with the Boy Scouts of America. Collin College, a community college with campuses across Collin County, confirmed that he attended the school at various times between Spring 2013 and 2018. He previously studied mechanical engineering at from 2014 to 2016. The university's admission's office confirmed he failed most of his classes. Jahn worked assembling and installing solar panels in D-FW about eight years ago, according to a former employer. Jahn's also listed previous employment at a in the state of Washington and at fast food and retail stores in . Collin County records show Jahn pleaded guilty to a felony in a Texas court 2016." name: Pete Buttigieg (via Democrats.org)
subject: A new era:
body:
---
Derek, With so much chaos and division in Washington, it is tempting to feel like the best we can do is to stop or slow down the damage. But this moment calls for so much more than that. The work ahead of us can’t just be about slowing, or even merely reversing, the destruction that is taking place. We are not doing all this work just to restore the old status quo. We must reimagine what must come next, and build something new — better and stronger than before. I believe a different kind of politics is possible: standing firm for what is right, while inviting people into our coalition instead of pushing them away. That’s why it’s so important to have a strong DNC. There is no substitute for strong party infrastructure, and right now the DNC is investing in every state party so that Democrats will have the resources they need to reach more people, not only in traditional battlegrounds but in every corner of the country. This is the long-term work required in a democracy — building organizational infrastructure that endures, growing our coalition, making sure more Americans feel included and represented. It rarely makes headlines, but this kind of work is indispensable in order to win the future. [**They can’t do it alone.
